t:
(a) Limitation.—Of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2014 for weapons and tracked combat vehicles, Army, for the procurement or upgrade of Stryker vehicles, not more than 75 percent may be obligated or expended until a period of 15 days has elapsed following the date on which the Secretary of the Army submits the report under subsection (b). 
    (b) Report Required.—The Secretary of the Army shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the status of the Stryker vehicle spare parts inventory located in Auburn, Washington, cited in the report of the Inspector General of the Department of Defense (number 2013–025) dated November 30, 2012. The report submitted under this subsection shall include the following:
        (1) The status of the implementation by the Secretary of the recommendations specified on pages 30 to 34 of the report by the Inspector General. 
        (2) The value of the parts remaining in warehouse that may still be used by the Secretary for the repair, upgrade, or reset of Stryker vehicles. 
        (3) The value of the parts remaining in the warehouse that are no longer usable by the Secretary for the repair, upgrade, or reset of Stryker vehicles. 
        (4) A cost estimate of the monthly cost of maintaining the inventory of such parts that are no longer usable by the Secretary. 
        (5) Any other matters the Secretary considers appropriate.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the required report and the 15-day waiting period before funds can be obligated amount to a consultation process. But the report goes only to the congressional defense committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. The section involves only the Secretary of the Army, the DoD Inspector General and Congress, with no public comment, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue for any outside party.
fable.s: The Secretary of the Army shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the status of the Stryker vehicle spare parts inventory located in Auburn, Washington

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary of the Army to submit a report to congressional defense committees. Congress and its committees are part of the federal government, so this interaction is internal to the government and does not involve outside parties. There is no consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary of the Army shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the status of the Stryker vehicle spare parts inventory

opus.w: The section limits spending until the Secretary of the Army sends a report to the congressional defense committees. It also refers to recommendations from the DoD Inspector General. All of these actors are inside the federal government, so this is reporting within the government, not outside participation. The waiting period before money can be spent looks procedural, but no non-federal party is consulted and none can comment or object.
opus.s: The Secretary of the Army shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the status of the Stryker vehicle spare parts inventory located in Auburn, Washington
opus.b:
1. The tempting reading is that the funding hold until a report is submitted counts as a formal process before a federal decision. That fails because the only people involved are the Secretary of the Army, the congressional defense committees and the DoD Inspector General. All of them are inside the federal government, and no state, company, expert or member of the public takes part.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Secretary of the Army to submit a report to congressional defense committees. Both the Secretary and Congress are inside the federal government. The definition explicitly excludes reports to Congress or its committees as participation, as they do not involve parties outside the federal government. There is no consultation with states, tribes, the public, or private entities.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of the Army shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the status of the Stryker vehicle spare parts inventory
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the report is submitted to "congressional defense committees," and since Congress is part of the federal government, this is internal coordination. However, the definition explicitly states that reports to Congress are "No" because Congress is inside the federal government. The key is whether *outside* parties are involved. Here, the only actors are the Secretary of the Army (federal) and the congressional committees (federal). There is no consultation with states, tribes, the public, or private entities. The "participation" definition requires interaction with people *outside* the government.
